You can open issues and propose changes in this repository, and we regularly update the remote server to include the latest version of this code. The remote server has [additional tools](#toolsets-only-available-in-the-remote-mcp-server) that are not available in the local MCP server, such as the `create_pull_request_with_copilot` tool for invoking Copilot coding agent. ## Remote MCP Toolsets Below is a table of available toolsets for the remote GitHub MCP Server. Each toolset is provided as a distinct URL so you can mix and match to create the perfect combination of tools for your use-case. Add `/readonly` to the end of any URL to restrict the tools in the toolset to only those that enable read access. E.g. "repos,issues". - Equivalent to `GITHUB_TOOLSETS` env var or `--toolsets` flag for Local server. - If the list is empty, default toolsets will be used. Invalid or unknown toolsets are silently ignored without error and will not prevent the server from starting. Whitespace is ignored. - `X-MCP-Tools`: Comma-separated list of tools to enable. E.g. "get_file_contents,issue_read,pull_request_read". - Equivalent to `GITHUB_TOOLS` env var or `--tools` flag for Local server. - Invalid tools will throw an error and prevent the server from starting. Whitespace is ignored. - `X-MCP-Readonly`: Enables only "read" tools. - Equivalent to `GITHUB_READ_ONLY` env var for Local server. - If this header is empty, "false", "f", "no", "n", "0", or "off" (ignoring whitespace and case), it will be interpreted as false. All other values are interpreted as true. - `X-MCP-Lockdown`: Enables lockdown mode, hiding public issue details created by users without push access. Lockdown mode is a best-effort content filter, not a security boundary. - Equivalent to `GITHUB_LOCKDOWN_MODE` env var for Local server. - If this header is empty, "false", "f", "no", "n", "0", or "off" (ignoring whitespace and case), it will be interpreted as false. All other values are interpreted as true. - Server-side lockdown configuration is an upper bound: if the operator has already enabled lockdown mode, this header cannot disable it for a request. The header can only enable (or redundantly re-enable) lockdown mode; it cannot relax lockdown mode below the operator's configuration. - `X-MCP-Insiders`: Enables insiders mode for early access to new features. - Equivalent to `GITHUB_INSIDERS` env var or `--insiders` flag for Local server. - If this header is empty, "false", "f", "no", "n", "0", or "off" (ignoring whitespace and case), it will be interpreted as false. All other values are interpreted as true. > **Looking for examples?** See the [Server Configuration Guide](./server-configuration.md) for common recipes like minimal setups, read-only mode, and combining tools with toolsets. Example: ```json { "type": "http", "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/", "headers": { "X-MCP-Toolsets": "repos,issues", "X-MCP-Readonly": "true", "X-MCP-Lockdown": "false" } } ``` ### Insiders Mode The remote GitHub MCP Server offers an insiders version with early access to new features and experimental tools. You can enable insiders mode in two ways: 1. **Via URL path** - Append `/insiders` to the URL: ```json { "type": "http", "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/insiders" } ``` 2. **Via header** - Set the `X-MCP-Insiders` header to `true`: ```json { "type": "http", "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/", "headers": { "X-MCP-Insiders": "true" } } ``` Both methods can be combined with other path modifiers (like `/readonly`) and headers. ### URL Path Parameters The Remote GitHub MCP server supports the following URL path patterns: - `/` - Default toolset (see ["default" toolset](../README.md#default-toolset)) - `/readonly` - Default toolset in read-only mode - `/insiders` - Default toolset with insiders mode enabled - `/readonly/insiders` - Default toolset in read-only mode with insiders mode enabled - `/x/all` - All available toolsets - `/x/all/readonly` - All available toolsets in read-only mode - `/x/all/insiders` - All available toolsets with insiders mode enabled - `/x/all/readonly/insiders` - All available toolsets in read-only mode with insiders mode enabled - `/x/{toolset}` - Single specific toolset - `/x/{toolset}/readonly` - Single specific toolset in read-only mode - `/x/{toolset}/insiders` - Single specific toolset with insiders mode enabled - `/x/{toolset}/readonly/insiders` - Single specific toolset in read-only mode with insiders mode enabled Note: `{toolset}` can only be a single toolset, not a comma-separated list. To combine multiple toolsets, use the `X-MCP-Toolsets` header instead. Path modifiers like `/readonly` and `/insiders` can be combined with the `X-MCP-Insiders` or `X-MCP-Readonly` headers. Example: ```json { "type": "http", "url": "https://api.githubcopilot.com/mcp/x/issues/readonly" } ```

## Design to code[​](#design-to-code "Direct link to Design to code")

Use these tools to bring designs from Figma into your codebase. `get_design_context` is the main tool. The others provide extra input for it, or are useful when a selection is too large or you need assets in a specific format.

### get\_design\_context[​](#get_design_context "Direct link to get_design_context")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design, Figma Make

Gets the [design context](/docs/figma-mcp-server/server-returning-web-code/) for a layer or selection in Figma. By default, the output is React and Tailwind, but you can ask for a different framework in your prompt.

If your design uses shader fills or effects, the output includes a lightweight Figma shader runtime. This requires HTML-in-Canvas to display correctly.

**Example prompts:**

*   **Change the framework**
    
    *   "Generate my Figma selection in Vue."
    *   "Generate my Figma selection in plain HTML and CSS."
    *   "Generate my Figma selection in iOS."
*   **Use your components**
    
    *   "Generate my Figma selection using components from src/components/ui."
*   **Combine both**
    
    *   "Generate my Figma selection using components from src/ui and style it with Tailwind."
*   **Implement a design that uses shaders**
    
    *   "Implement this Figma frame in React using the included shader runtime."

tip

Set up [Code Connect](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/23920389749655-Code-Connect) for the best component reuse. You can map more than one codebase to the same Figma components, such as React and SwiftUI.

*   The **desktop server** uses the Code Connect mapping you've selected in Dev Mode.
*   With the **remote server**, ask your agent to set the `clientFrameworks` parameter to your Code Connect label, such as `React` or `SwiftUI`.

On Professional plans, only one framework can be active at a time, so the MCP server returns connections for that framework only. Organization and Enterprise plans can have multiple active frameworks.

note

Prompting with your current selection only works with the desktop server. With the remote server, include a link to a frame or layer in your prompt.

### get\_metadata[​](#get_metadata "Direct link to get_metadata")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Returns a lightweight XML outline of your selection with basic properties only: layer IDs, names, types, positions, and sizes. Your agent can use this outline to call `get_design_context` on only the parts it needs. This is useful for very large designs, where `get_design_context` returns too much at once.

Without a node ID, `get_metadata` returns a list of the file's top-level pages. Your agent can use this list to choose a page to explore. If the node ID is invalid, the error response also includes the page list.

For more detail about each page, such as child counts and top-level node types, your agent can use [`use_figma`](#use_figma) to read the file structure directly.

### get\_screenshot[​](#get_screenshot "Direct link to get_screenshot")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design, FigJam, Figma Slides

Takes a screenshot of your selection so your agent can see the design. This helps the generated code match the layout more closely. Screenshots use more tokens, so leave this on unless you're concerned about token limits.

### download\_assets[​](#download_assets "Direct link to download_assets")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design, FigJam, Figma Slides

Downloads assets from a Figma file for up to 20 nodes per call. It returns temporary URLs your agent uses to fetch the files. Each call returns both:

*   **Export renders**: Each node rendered as PNG, JPG, SVG, or PDF. Uses the node's export settings in Figma if it has them. Otherwise, it uses the `defaultFormat` and `defaultScale` parameters (0.01x to 4x). Without export settings, renders at 1x are capped at about 4,096 px on the longest edge.
*   **Raw source images**: The original uploaded image files (JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP) used as fills anywhere inside the node, without re-rendering. Returns up to 20 images per call. If there are more, the response includes `rawImagesTruncated: true`; try a more specific child node.

**When to use `download_assets` or `get_screenshot`**

Use `get_screenshot` when your agent needs to _see_ a design. Use `download_assets` when your agent needs to _deliver_ an asset, export in a specific format, or move images between files.

**Example prompts:**

*   **Export assets in a specific format**
    
    *   "Export these icons from my Figma file as SVGs."
    *   "Download the hero image from this frame as a JPG."
    *   "Export this component as a PDF."
*   **Get original source images**
    
    *   "Grab the original photos from this mockup."
    *   "Extract the source images from this frame so I can move them to another file."
*   **Move images between files**
    
    *   "Copy the images from this file into my other Figma file."

### get\_variable\_defs[​](#get_variable_defs "Direct link to get_variable_defs")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Returns the variables and styles used in your selection, such as colors, spacing, and typography.

**Example prompts:**

*   **List all variables used**
    
    *   "Get the variables used in my Figma selection."
*   **Focus on a specific type**
    
    *   "What color and spacing variables are used in my Figma selection?"
*   **Get names and values**
    
    *   "List the variable names and their values used in my Figma selection."

### get\_motion\_context[​](#get_motion_context "Direct link to get_motion_context")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Returns animation data for an animated node so your agent can recreate the motion in code. The response includes:

*   A list of animated nodes
*   Keyframe tracks with easing curves
*   Ready-to-use CSS `@keyframes` and [Motion](https://motion.dev) code snippets
*   Hints about which nodes animate together

Use `get_motion_context` after `get_design_context` when a design includes animation, using the same node ID. `get_design_context` provides the static structure and styles, and `get_motion_context` adds the motion. To get motion data for every animated layer inside the selection in one call, set `recursive: true`.

### get\_figjam[​](#get_figjam "Direct link to get_figjam")

**Supported file types:** FigJam

Returns an XML outline of FigJam diagrams, similar to [`get_metadata`](#get_metadata), plus screenshots of the nodes.

## Code to design[​](#code-to-design "Direct link to Code to design")

Use these tools to write into Figma: create and edit files, layers, and content from code or from a description.

tip

These tools work best with a [skill](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/39166810751895). Use `figma-use` for Figma Design, `figma-use-figjam` for FigJam, and `figma-use-slides` for Figma Slides.

### use\_figma[​](#use_figma "Direct link to use_figma")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design, FigJam, Figma Slides, Figma Specs

The general-purpose tool for writing to Figma files. Your agent can use it to create, edit, delete, or inspect content:

*   **Figma Design**: Pages, frames, components, variants, variables, styles, text, images, and more
*   **FigJam**: Stickies, sections, connectors, shapes, tables, code blocks, and more
*   **Figma Slides**: Slides, layouts, text, images, and other deck content
*   **Figma Specs**: Read, create, and edit specs, including specs embedded in Figma Design and FigJam files. Requires the `figma-spec` skill.

When relevant, your agent checks your design system and existing file content before creating anything from scratch.

note

`use_figma` can work with images that are already in your file, but it can't add new ones. To add new images, your agent uses [`upload_assets`](#upload_assets). To create a new image first, it can use [`generate_image`](#generate_image).

note

Figma Specs is in open beta and is only available on plans where Specs is turned on.

**Example prompts:**

*   **Create or update designs**
    
    *   "Add a new frame to my Figma file."
    *   "Update the button component to use the correct fill color."
*   **Set up variables or styles**
    
    *   "Create a color variable collection from my design tokens."
    *   "Set up spacing variables in my Figma file."
*   **Build or update components and variants**
    
    *   "Generate variants for the card component."
    *   "Sync my Figma components with my latest code changes."
*   **Fix layout or visual issues**
    
    *   "Fix the auto layout spacing on the nav component."
    *   "Update the typography styles to match the design spec."
*   **Create or update FigJam boards**
    
    *   "Organize this FigJam board into sections."
    *   "Add stickies and connectors to summarize this project brief."
*   **Read and update specs**
    
    *   "Read the spec in <Figma file URL> and implement the checkout requirements."
    *   "Add the edge cases we found today to the open questions section of this spec."

### generate\_figma\_design[​](#generate_figma_design "Direct link to generate_figma_design")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

note

Available with [select MCP clients](/docs/figma-mcp-server/#h_01K25F7RBRZKCATVJHNXCS6KXW). This tool doesn't count toward the standard Figma MCP server rate limits.

Sends the live UI of your web apps and sites to Figma as design layers. You can send it to:

*   A new Figma Design file
*   An existing Figma Design file
*   Your clipboard

New files are created in your team or organization drafts. To add to an existing file, you need edit access. Your seat type determines what you can create or edit.

For step-by-step instructions, see [Code to canvas](/docs/figma-mcp-server/code-to-canvas/).

### create\_new\_file[​](#create_new_file "Direct link to create_new_file")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Creates a blank Figma Design, FigJam, or Figma Slides file in your drafts. If you belong to more than one plan, your agent asks which team or organization to use.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Create a new Figma file called 'Homepage Redesign.'"
*   "Create a new FigJam board for our project planning session."
*   "Create a new Figma Slides deck for our Q3 review."

### upload\_assets[​](#upload_assets "Direct link to upload_assets")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design, FigJam, Figma Slides

Uploads images and SVGs into a Figma file. Supports PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, and SVG files up to 10 MB each, and up to 60 files per call.

*   **Images**: If you include a link to a specific layer, the image is added as that layer's fill. Otherwise, the tool creates new frames with the images as fills.
*   **SVGs**: Added as editable vector layers, not image fills.

To move images between Figma files, your agent uses [`download_assets`](#download_assets) to get the original images, then `upload_assets` to add them to the other file.

### generate\_diagram[​](#generate_diagram "Direct link to generate_diagram")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Generates a FigJam diagram from a description or from Mermaid syntax. You don't need to write Mermaid yourself: describe the diagram you want and your agent generates the syntax. Diagrams can go in a new FigJam file or an existing one.

**Supported diagram types:** Flowcharts, Gantt charts, state diagrams, sequence diagrams, architecture diagrams, and entity relationship diagrams (ERDs)

**Example prompts:**

*   **Generate a diagram from a description**
    
    *   "Create a flowchart for the user authentication flow using the Figma MCP generate\_diagram tool."
    *   "Generate a Gantt chart for the project timeline using the Figma MCP generate\_diagram tool."
    *   "Generate an ERD for a blog database with users, posts, and comments using the Figma MCP generate\_diagram tool."
*   **Convert existing Mermaid syntax**
    
    *   "Create a diagram from this Mermaid syntax: …"

tip

Your agent usually uses this tool automatically when you ask for a diagram. To make sure it does, include "using the Figma MCP generate\_diagram tool" in your prompt.

### html\_to\_figma[​](#html_to_figma "Direct link to html_to_figma")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Converts an HTML document into design layers in a Figma Design file. Use it for HTML from your codebase or HTML your agent creates, such as a visual style sheet based on your design tokens.

*   The result is plain layers. It doesn't use your components, libraries, or variables. To build with your design system, your agent uses [`use_figma`](#use_figma) instead.
*   It doesn't run your app or capture a live site. To capture a running web app, your agent uses [`generate_figma_design`](#generate_figma_design). To capture an external website, use the [Figma Chrome extension](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/9067379354135-Figma-Chrome-extension).
*   The HTML must be self-contained, with CSS and images included in the document. External links aren't loaded. The document can be up to 50 MB.
*   Your agent can choose specific elements, like every card on a page, to turn each one into its own frame, up to 20 per call.

If you don't choose where to add the layers, they're added to a new page in the file.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Create a style sheet from our design tokens and add it to <Figma file URL>."
*   "Turn the cards in this HTML file into separate frames in <Figma file URL>."

### generate\_image[​](#generate_image "Direct link to generate_image")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design, FigJam, Figma Slides

Generates an image from a text description and places it in the file specified by `fileKey`. Omit `nodeId` to create a new image-filled frame, or provide it to replace an existing image fill without resizing the node. If you need a new file, call `create_new_file` first.

The tool checks AI permissions and credits against the destination file and returns its file key, the placed node ID, model, width, and height. Use `download_assets` to download the image.

*   **Uses Figma AI credits.** Each image uses [AI credits](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/33459875669015) from the destination file's plan, and the cost depends on the image model.
*   **Size is approximate.** The requested width and height set the aspect ratio, but the final size may be different.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Generate a hero image of a mountain trail at sunrise for our landing page."
*   "Create a product photo for this card and add it to <link to selection>."

## Design systems and Code Connect[​](#design-systems-and-code-connect "Direct link to Design systems and Code Connect")

Use these tools to find existing design system assets and to map Figma components to code components in your codebase.

### get\_libraries[​](#get_libraries "Direct link to get_libraries")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Lists the libraries for a Figma file in two groups: libraries already added to the file, and libraries you can add, such as Community UI kits and organization libraries. Each result includes the library's name, key, description, and source. Your agent uses this with [`search_design_system`](#search_design_system).

### search\_design\_system[​](#search_design_system "Direct link to search_design_system")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Searches all connected libraries for components, variables, and styles that match a text query, so your agent can reuse what already exists instead of creating new elements. Your agent can send several searches in one call.

**Example prompts:**

*   **Find components**
    
    *   "Search for a button component in my design system."
    *   "Find a card component I can use for this layout."
*   **Find variables**
    
    *   "Search for the primary color variable in my design system."
    *   "Find spacing variables in my design libraries."
*   **Narrow by type**
    
    *   "Search for icon styles in my design system."

### get\_code\_connect\_map[​](#get_code_connect_map "Direct link to get_code_connect_map")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Returns the Code Connect mappings for the instances in your selection. For each instance, the response includes:

*   `componentName`: The component's name in your codebase
*   `source`: Where the component lives in your codebase (file path or URL)
*   `snippet`, `snippetImports`, `snippetNestedFunctions`: Code snippet data, when available
*   `version`: Where the mapping came from, such as the Code Connect UI or CLI
*   `label`: The framework label, such as `React`, when available

Each selected instance appears separately, even if several use the same component. Nested components with their own mappings, such as an icon inside a button, may also be included.

With the remote server, your agent can use `clientFrameworks` and `clientLanguages` to choose which mappings are returned.

### add\_code\_connect\_map[​](#add_code_connect_map "Direct link to add_code_connect_map")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Maps a Figma component to its code component in your codebase. Mappings improve design-to-code output and help your agent use the exact components in your project.

### Tools used by Figma[​](#figma-prompted-tools "Direct link to Tools used by Figma")

Figma or the `figma-code-connect` skill uses these tools as part of a larger Code Connect workflow. You don't need to call them directly.

*   `get_code_connect_suggestions`: Detects Figma components and suggests which code components to map them to.
*   `get_context_for_code_connect`: Returns component details used to generate Code Connect templates, including properties, variant options, and nested instances and text layers.
*   `send_code_connect_mappings`: Confirms the mappings suggested by `get_code_connect_suggestions`.

All three support Figma Design files.

## Generative plugins and shaders[​](#generative-plugins-and-shaders "Direct link to Generative plugins and shaders")

Use these tools to read and write the source code behind generative plugins, shader fills, and shader effects that you build by prompting Figma Agent.

Resource

List

Read

Create

Update

Generative plugin

list\_generative\_plugins

get\_generative\_plugin

create\_generative\_plugin

update\_generative\_plugin

Shader (effect or fill)

list\_shaders  
,  
list\_file\_shaders

create\_shader

update\_shader

caution

Creating and updating requires a skill. Your agent must load `figma-generative-plugins` before creating or updating plugins, and `figma-shaders` before creating or updating shaders.

These rules apply to all tools in this group:

*   **Access**: You can read the code for any shader, but only for your own plugins. Every response includes an `owner` field: your email, `figma`, or a publisher handle.
*   **Create returns a starter**: `create_generative_plugin` and `create_shader` create a working starter, not a finished resource. Your agent follows up with the matching update tool.
*   **Updates replace whole files**: Updates must include the complete contents of each file, not just the changes. Files you don't include stay as they are. You can't add new files. Shaders have `main.ts`; plugins have `code.ts` and `ui.html`.
*   **Plan keys come from [`whoami`](#whoami)**: Creating a plugin or shader requires a `planKey`, copied exactly from the plans `whoami` returns.

note

`list_shaders` and `get_shader` replace `list_shader_effects`, `list_shader_fills`, `get_shader_effect`, and `get_shader_fill`, which are deprecated.

### list\_generative\_plugins[​](#list_generative_plugins "Direct link to list_generative_plugins")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Lists the generative plugins in your account library, including Figma's own plugins. Generative plugins are runnable tools that change the canvas. They're separate from shader effects and fills.

**Parameters:** `cursor` (optional): The `nextCursor` value from a previous call, to get the next page. Leave it out to get the first page.

**Response:** Each plugin's `id`, `name`, `description`, and `owner`, plus `nextCursor` if there are more pages. `owner` is your email for plugins you own, or a public publisher handle.

**Example prompts:**

*   "List my generative plugins."
*   "Find my layer-renaming plugin so I can update it."

### get\_generative\_plugin[​](#get_generative_plugin "Direct link to get_generative_plugin")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Reads a generative plugin from your account library.

**Parameters:**

*   `id`: The plugin ID, from `list_generative_plugins`
*   `version` (optional): A 40-character commit SHA. Defaults to the latest built version.
*   `includeSource` (optional, default `false`): Includes each file's source in the response instead of a URI. Only for clients that can't read MCP resources. Limited to 100 files and 1,000,000 bytes total; the response says which limit was reached.

**Response:** The plugin's `name`, `description`, `owner`, `version`, and a list of its source files as `{ filename, bytes, uri }`. By default, your agent reads each file from its `uri` as an MCP resource.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Show me the source for my layer-renaming plugin."
*   "Get version <commit SHA> of my layer-renaming plugin."

### create\_generative\_plugin[​](#create_generative_plugin "Direct link to create_generative_plugin")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Creates a new generative plugin in your account library. The plugin starts as a working starter that draws a square. Your agent then uses `update_generative_plugin` to add the behavior you want.

**Requires the `figma-generative-plugins` skill.**

**Parameters:**

*   `name`: The plugin's display name
*   `description`: A short description of what the plugin does
*   `planKey`: The plan that owns the plugin, in the format `(team|organization)::<numeric-id>`. Copied from [`whoami`](#whoami).

**Response:** The new plugin's ID, or an error message.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Create a new generative plugin called 'Layer renamer' in my team plan."
*   "Create a generative plugin, then update it to batch-rename my selected layers."

### update\_generative\_plugin[​](#update_generative_plugin "Direct link to update_generative_plugin")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Updates an existing generative plugin. Figma builds, versions, and deploys the update.

**Requires the `figma-generative-plugins` skill.**

**Parameters:**

*   `id`: The plugin ID
*   `commitMessage` (required): A Git commit message describing the change
*   `files` (optional, default `[]`): A list of `{ path, content }`. `path` must be `code.ts` or `ui.html`, and `content` must be the complete file. Your agent should read the current source with `get_generative_plugin` first.
*   `metadata` (optional): `{ name, description }` to change the plugin's name or description. Send an empty `files` list to update only the metadata.

**Response:** The new version, or an error. A successful response may not include a version, so any response without an error means the update worked. If the build fails, the response includes compiler output; your agent should make the smallest fix it identifies and try once more.

`code.ts` runs in the plugin sandbox and is the only file that can call `figma.*`. `ui.html` is the plugin panel and the only file with DOM access; it uses PropsKit `fig-*` elements. You can't replace `manifest.json`.

### list\_shaders[​](#list_shaders "Direct link to list_shaders")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Lists the shader effects and shader fills in your account library.

**Parameters:** `cursor` (optional): The `nextCursor` value from a previous call, to get the next page.

**Response:** Each shader's `id`, `name`, `description`, `owner`, and `type`, plus `nextCursor` if there are more pages. `type` is `"effect"` (changes the layer beneath it) or `"fill"` (generates its own pixels). `owner` is your email for shaders you own, or `figma` for Figma's shaders.

**Example prompts:**

*   "List the shaders in my library."
*   "Find my star field shader."

### get\_shader[​](#get_shader "Direct link to get_shader")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Reads a shader effect or fill from your account library.

**Parameters:**

*   `id`: The shader ID, from `list_shaders`
*   `version` (optional): A 40-character commit SHA. Defaults to the latest built version.
*   `includeSource` (optional, default `false`): Includes each file's source in the response instead of a URI. Only for clients that can't read MCP resources. Limited to 100 files and 1,000,000 bytes total.

**Response:** The shader's `name`, `description`, `owner`, `type`, `version`, and a list of its source files as `{ filename, bytes, uri }`.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Show me the source for my star field shader."
*   "Get version <commit SHA> of my star field shader."

### create\_shader[​](#create_shader "Direct link to create_shader")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Creates a new shader effect or fill in your account library. Like `create_generative_plugin`, it creates a working starter. Your agent then uses `update_shader` to add the behavior you want.

**Requires the `figma-shaders` skill.**

**Parameters:**

*   `name`: The shader's display name
*   `description`: A one-line description of what it does
*   `planKey`: The plan that owns the shader, in the format `(team|organization)::<numeric-id>`. Copied from [`whoami`](#whoami).
*   `kind`: `"effect"` to change the layer beneath it, or `"fill"` to generate its own pixels

**Response:** The new shader's ID, or an error message.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Create a shader fill called 'Topographic contours' in my team plan."
*   "Create a shader effect called 'Chromatic blur' in my organization plan."

### update\_shader[​](#update_shader "Direct link to update_shader")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Updates an existing shader effect or fill. Figma builds, versions, and deploys the update.

**Requires the `figma-shaders` skill.**

**Parameters:**

*   `id`: The shader ID
*   `kind`: `"effect"` or `"fill"`. Must match the existing shader; you can't change the kind.
*   `commitMessage` (required): A Git commit message describing the change
*   `files` (optional, default `[]`): A list of `{ path, content }`. `path` must be `main.ts`, and `content` must be the complete file. Send an empty list to update only the metadata.
*   `metadata` (optional): `{ name, description }` to change the shader's name or description

**Response:** The new version, or an error. A successful response may not include a version, so any response without an error means the update worked. If the build fails, the response includes compiler output; your agent should make the smallest fix it identifies and try once more.

### list\_file\_shaders[​](#list_file_shaders "Direct link to list_file_shaders")

**Supported file types:** Figma Design

Lists the shader effects and fills used in a specific Figma file. Use this to read a shader you don't own: you only need view access to the file. Source code is returned for the exact shader version the file uses, so what you read matches what the file shows.

**Parameters:** `fileKey`: The key of the Figma file

**Response:** Up to 100 shaders. For each shader:

*   `id`: The shader ID
*   `name`: Display name
*   `description`: Short description
*   `type`: `"effect"` or `"fill"`
*   `version`: The exact version the file uses
*   `published`: Whether this is a published library version
*   `truncated`: `true` if the shader's file list reached its 10,000-file limit
*   `files`: The shader's source files as `{ filename, uri }`

A top-level `truncated: true` means at least one shader couldn't be returned, including when the file uses more than 100 shaders.

**Example prompts:**

*   "What shaders are used in this Figma file?"
*   "Show me the source for the background shader in this file."

## Figma Make and code layers[​](#figma-make-code-layers "Direct link to Figma Make and code layers")

Use these tools to bring code projects into Figma and keep building them with the Figma Make agent. Your agent can create a Figma Make file or a code layer in a Figma Design file, send prompts, and check progress.

tip

Mention “code layer” in your prompt when you want your agent to bring a project into a Figma Design file.

### send\_code\_to\_figma[​](#send_code_to_figma "Direct link to send_code_to_figma")

**Supported file types:** Figma Make, Figma Design

Imports a project from your computer into Figma. In a Figma Make file, the project becomes the file's code. In a Figma Design file, it becomes a new code layer. It doesn't create design layers.

*   Requires edit access to the file.
*   Your agent packages the project as a .zip, .tar.gz, or .tgz file and uploads it.
*   The first import doesn't use Figma AI credits. Prompting and later changes do.

After importing, open the file to preview the project.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Import this project into <Figma file URL> as a code layer."
*   "Bring the checkout flow from this repo into a new Figma Make file."

note

Importing a project with send\_code\_to\_figma doesn't use credits, but prompting and later changes do.

## Account[​](#account "Direct link to Account")

### whoami[​](#whoami "Direct link to whoami")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Returns details about the Figma account you're signed in with:

*   Your email address
*   All the plans you belong to
*   Your seat type on each plan

Your agent needs this to create generative plugins and shaders, which require a `planKey` from the plans list.

## Figma Weave[​](#weave-tools "Direct link to Figma Weave")

Use these tools to run Figma Weave from your agent. Your agent can run a published Weave tool, or [run a Weave model directly](#weave_find_model) without publishing a tool first. In Weave, a “tool” is a published Weave workflow, not an MCP tool.

note

You need a paid standalone Figma Weave account to run Weave tools. Runs use your Weave credits, not your Figma AI credits. Before a paid run, your agent shows you the cost and asks you to confirm.

### weave\_list\_tools[​](#weave_list_tools "Direct link to weave_list_tools")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Lists the Weave tools you can run in your active Weave workspace: your own tools, tools shared with the workspace, and tools shared with you by email. Private tools aren't included.

**Parameters:** `search` (optional): Text to match against tool names, not case-sensitive.

**Response:** The most recently updated tools and the total number available. For each tool: its name, creator, last updated date, and a link to open it in Weave.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Show me the Weave tools I can run."
*   "Find the 'image generator' Weave tool."

tip

If you already have a Weave link (`app.weavy.ai/tool/<id>` or `app.weavy.ai/flow/<id>`), the `<id>` is the tool's `recipeId`. Your agent can skip this step and go straight to `weave_get_tool_inputs`.

### weave\_get\_tool\_inputs[​](#weave_get_tool_inputs "Direct link to weave_get_tool_inputs")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Gets the inputs a Weave tool needs to run. Your agent uses this before `weave_run_tool`.

**Parameters:**

*   `recipeId`: The Weave tool ID, from `weave_list_tools`
*   `version` (optional): The tool version. Defaults to the latest.

**Response:** The tool `version`, a summary of its `outputs`, and a list of `inputs` with each input's `nodeId`, `name`, `type`, `required`, `description`, `options`, `range`, `isIterator`, and `default`.

**Example prompts:**

*   "What inputs does the 'image generator' Weave tool take?"
*   "Show me the inputs and their defaults for this Weave tool."

### weave\_upload\_asset[​](#weave_upload_asset "Direct link to weave_upload_asset")

**Supported file types:** Images (PNG, JPG, WebP, HEIC), video (MP4, MOV, WebM), audio (MP3, WAV, OGG, and other common formats), and 3D models (GLB, OBJ, FBX, PLY)

Uploads an attached file so it can be used as an input for `weave_run_tool`. Files that already have a public HTTPS URL don't need to be uploaded.

**Parameters:** `recipeId`: The Weave tool the file is for

**Response:** A single-use `submitUrl` for the upload. After the upload, the file's permanent hosted URL.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Use this image as the reference input for the Weave tool."
*   "Upload this file to Weave so I can run a tool on it."

### weave\_run\_tool[​](#weave_run_tool "Direct link to weave_run_tool")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Runs a Weave tool. Your agent uses `weave_get_tool_inputs` first, then checks progress with `weave_get_tool_run_output`.

Because runs use credits, the tool won't start until it has what it needs. If inputs are missing or invalid, it returns `inputs_required`. If the run has a cost, it returns `cost_confirmation_required` with the number of credits. Your agent confirms with you before running.

**Parameters:**

*   `recipeId`: The Weave tool ID
*   `version` (optional): The tool version
*   `inputs` (optional): A list of `{ nodeId, value }`
*   `numberOfRuns` (optional): 1 to 10
*   `acknowledgedCost` (optional): Set after you confirm the cost

**Response:** The `runIds` of the runs that started, or a status explaining what's needed.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Run the 'image generator' Weave tool with the prompt 'a cat.'"
*   "Run this Weave tool 3 times."

### weave\_get\_tool\_run\_output[​](#weave_get_tool_run_output "Direct link to weave_get_tool_run_output")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Gets the status and output of Weave runs.

**Parameters:** `recipeId`, and optionally `runIds`

**Response:** For each run: its status (`RUNNING`, `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, or `CANCELED`), progress, any errors, and the output once it's complete.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Is my Weave run done yet?"
*   "Show me the output of my last Weave run."

### weave\_cancel\_tool\_run[​](#weave_cancel_tool_run "Direct link to weave_cancel_tool_run")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Cancels one or more in-progress runs. You can't undo this.

**Parameters:** `recipeId`, and optionally `runIds`. Leave out `runIds` to cancel all runs.

**Response:** Confirmation of the canceled runs.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Cancel that Weave run."
*   "Cancel all my running Weave tool runs."

### weave\_find\_model[​](#weave_find_model "Direct link to weave_find_model")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Finds a Weave model by name so your agent can run it with `weave_run_model`. Use this when you name a model in your prompt. If the name matches more than one model, your agent shows you the options.

**Parameters:** `query`: The model name, as you said it

**Response:** The model, its approximate cost, and the inputs and settings it accepts, including which are required and any allowed values. If more than one model matches, a short list of options.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Run Nano Banana 2 on this image."
*   "Make a video of this product photo with Veo 3."

### weave\_run\_model[​](#weave_run_model "Direct link to weave_run_model")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Runs a Weave model directly, without a published Weave tool. Your agent uses `weave_find_model` first, then checks progress with `weave_get_model_run_output`.

Because runs use Weave credits, your agent shows you the cost and asks you to approve every run, including reruns. If an input is missing, your agent asks you for it.

**Parameters:**

*   `id`: The model ID, from `weave_find_model`
*   `input`: The inputs and settings to run with. For images, video, or other media, your agent uses a file uploaded with `weave_upload_asset`, an earlier run's output, or a public HTTPS link.
*   `acknowledgedCost` (optional): Set after you approve the cost

**Response:** A prediction ID to check progress, or the cost to approve before the run starts.

### weave\_get\_model\_run\_output[​](#weave_get_model_run_output "Direct link to weave_get_model_run_output")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Gets the status and output of model runs started with `weave_run_model`. For runs of published Weave tools, your agent uses `weave_get_tool_run_output` instead.

**Parameters:** `predictionIds`: The prediction IDs returned by `weave_run_model`

**Response:** The status and output of each run, with links to download the results.

**Example prompts:**

*   "Is my video done yet?"
*   "Download the images from my last model run."

## MCP prompts[​](#prompts "Direct link to MCP prompts")

[MCP prompts](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/latest/server/prompts) are different from the prompts you type to chat with your agent. They're built into the MCP server, and you run them with a command in your client. The command depends on the client, and not all clients support MCP prompts. Check your client's documentation.

### create\_design\_system\_rules[​](#create_design_system_rules "Direct link to create_design_system_rules")

**Supported file types:** No file needed

Creates a rules file that gives your agent the context it needs to turn designs into code that fits your codebase, design system, and tech stack.

After running the prompt, save the result to your project's `rules/` or `instructions/` folder so your agent can use it when generating code.

# Preset Tool Collections Reference

This document provides detailed information about all preset tool collections available in lark-mcp. Presets are predefined sets of tools that can be enabled together for specific use cases.

## Overview

If you have no special requirements, you can keep the default preset to use common functions. When you need fine control or want to understand the complete list, please refer to the preset table below.

## How to Use Presets

To use a preset, specify it in the `-t` parameter:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lark-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",
        "mcp",
        "-a", "<your_app_id>",
        "-s", "<your_app_secret>",
        "-t", "preset.light"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

You can also combine presets with individual tools:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "lark-mcp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@larksuiteoapi/lark-mcp",
        "mcp",
        "-a", "<your_app_id>",
        "-s", "<your_app_secret>",
        "-t", "preset.light,im.v1.message.create"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

## Preset Tool Collections

| Tool Name | Function Description | preset.light | preset.default (Default) | preset.im.default | preset.base.default | preset.base.batch | preset.doc.default | preset.task.default | preset.calendar.default |
| --- | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| im.v1.chat.create | Create a group chat | | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | |
| im.v1.chat.list | Get group chat list | | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | |
| im.v1.chat.search | Search group chats | ✓ | | | | | | | |
| im.v1.chatMembers.get | Get group members | | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | |
| im.v1.message.create | Send messages | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | |
| im.v1.message.list | Get message list | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | |
| bitable.v1.app.create | Create base | | ✓ | | ✓ | ✓ | | | |
| bitable.v1.appTable.create | Create base data table | | ✓ | | ✓ | ✓ | | | |
| bitable.v1.appTable.list | Get base data table list | | ✓ | | ✓ | ✓ | | | |
| bitable.v1.appTableField.list | Get base data table field list | | ✓ | | ✓ | ✓ | | | |
| bitable.v1.appTableRecord.search | Search base data table records | ✓ | ✓ | | ✓ | ✓ | | | |
| bitable.v1.appTableRecord.create | Create base data table records | | ✓ | | ✓ | | | | |
| bitable.v1.appTableRecord.batchCreate | Batch create base data table records | ✓ | | | | ✓ | | | |
| bitable.v1.appTableRecord.update | Update base data table records | | ✓ | | ✓ | | | | |
| bitable.v1.appTableRecord.batchUpdate | Batch update base data table records | | | | | ✓ | | | |
| docx.v1.document.rawContent | Get document content | ✓ | ✓ | | | | ✓ | | |
| docx.builtin.import | Import documents | ✓ | ✓ | | | | ✓ | | |
| docx.builtin.search | Search documents | ✓ | ✓ | | | | ✓ | | |
| drive.v1.permissionMember.create | Add collaborator permissions | | ✓ | | | | ✓ | | |
| wiki.v2.space.getNode | Get Wiki node | ✓ | ✓ | | | | ✓ | | |
| wiki.v1.node.search | Search Wiki nodes | | ✓ | | | | ✓ | | |
| contact.v3.user.batchGetId | Batch get user IDs | ✓ | ✓ | | | | | | |
| task.v2.task.create | Create task | | | | | | | ✓ | |
| task.v2.task.patch | Modify task | | | | | | | ✓ | |
| task.v2.task.addMembers | Add task members | | | | | | | ✓ | |
| task.v2.task.addReminders | Add task reminders | | | | | | | ✓ | |
| calendar.v4.calendarEvent.create | Create calendar event | | | | | | | | ✓ |
| calendar.v4.calendarEvent.patch | Modify calendar event | | | | | | | | ✓ |
| calendar.v4.calendarEvent.get | Get calendar event | | | | | | | | ✓ |
| calendar.v4.freebusy.list | Query free/busy status | | | | | | | | ✓ |
| calendar.v4.calendar.primary | Get primary calendar | | | | | | | | ✓ |

> **Note**: In the table, "✓" indicates the tool is included in that preset. Using `-t preset.xxx` will enable tools marked with "✓" in the corresponding column.

## Preset Descriptions

### preset.light
A minimal preset that includes only the most essential tools for basic messaging and document operations. Ideal for lightweight integrations.

### preset.default (Default)
The default preset that includes commonly used tools across messaging, documents, databases, and collaboration. Recommended for most users.

### preset.im.default
Focused on instant messaging functionality, including chat creation, member management, and message handling.

### preset.base.default
Includes basic database operations with BitTable (multi-dimensional tables) for data management scenarios.

### preset.base.batch
Specialized for batch operations on BitTable data, useful for bulk data processing.

### preset.doc.default
Document-focused preset including document reading, importing, searching, and collaboration features.

### preset.task.default
Task management focused preset for creating, modifying, and managing tasks with reminders and members.

### preset.calendar.default
Calendar management preset for creating, modifying events, and querying availability.
